answer: The pulse detector writes to cedar, and vault publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 99 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 188 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 28 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
